Assert that a unit's spells leave no gaps

Source: R/ensure_no_gaps.R
ensure_no_gaps.Rd

A checkpoint for spell data that should cover a unit without a break: everyone resident has an address every day, an insured person a policy, a dwelling an owner. A spell that starts later than the day after the unit's earlier spells have ended leaves days that no spell covers. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_no_gaps(
  data,
  id,
  start,
  end,
  max_gap = 0,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

start, end

Columns with the first and last period of each spell (dates, or integers such as years).

max_gap

The longest gap that is accepted, in days (or periods). The default 0 accepts none. As in merge_spells(), max_gap = 1 lets a spell start two days after the previous one ended.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when there are gaps and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

It is the counterpart of ensure_no_overlap(): that a unit is in at most one spell at a time, and here in at least one, between its first start and its last end. Together they say exactly one. The time before a unit's first spell and after its last is not a gap; compare those with birth, death or migration dates with ensure_within().

On failure the spell that starts after each gap is reported, with a gap column prepended holding the number of days (or periods) that no spell covers before it. The spell that ended last before the gap is the one with the latest end among the unit's earlier spells, not always the row above.

Spells are closed intervals, as in ensure_no_overlap(): a spell ending 31 January and one starting 1 February leave no gap, one starting 2 February leaves a gap of one day. A missing end means an ongoing spell, and nothing after its start is a gap. Rows with a missing start, or an end before the start, are ignored, as in describe_spells(); find them with ensure_valid_spells().

See also

describe_spells() to count the gaps and their lengths first, ensure_no_overlap() for the opposite rule, merge_spells() to join spells across short gaps, checkpoints.

Examples

addresses <- data.frame(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  start = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-07-04")),
  end   = as.Date(c("2020-12-31", NA,           "2020-06-30", "2021-12-31"))
)

# b has no address on 1, 2 and 3 July 2020
ensure_no_gaps(addresses, cpr, start, end)
#> Warning: Gaps between spells per cpr
#> ℹ 1 row
#>   In 1 unit
#>   Gap length: shortest 3, median 3, longest 3
#> ℹ The rows:
#>       gap cpr   start      end
#>     <int> <chr> <date>     <date>
#>   1     3 b     2020-07-04 2021-12-31
#> ℹ To join spells across gaps up to a length you choose: merge_spells(addresses, cpr, start, end, max_gap = <length>)

# Accept up to a week without an address
ensure_no_gaps(addresses, cpr, start, end, max_gap = 7)
#> ✔ No gaps between spells longer than 7 per cpr
